items.title: Johor JPJ collects RM1.17m in VEP summonses from January to October
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — The Johor Road Transport Department (JPJ) issued 7,804 summonses totalling RM1.17 million through the implementation of the Vehicle Entry Permit (VEP) from January to October 18, according to its director Zulkarnain Yasin. He said this was the result of inspections on 120,740 vehicles at the state’s two land entry points — the Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) and Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB). He said enforcement operations were conducted continuously at the two entry points.

items.title: From collecting coins for rice and petrol to a Mitsubishi XForce
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT: Syahidatul Azimah Azmi, who once collected coins with her husband to buy rice and petrol, was moved to tears when he surprised her with a Mitsubishi XForce. According to Harian Metro, Syahidatul, 34, said the gift from her husband, Abubakar Sanusi, 30, reminded her of how far they had come since tying the knot in September 2016, and of the challenges they had overcome together. She said she had never expected to receive the Mitsubishi XForce, as their Proton Persona, which they had used since 2012, before their marriage, had become increasingly prone to breakdowns, making daily travel difficult.

items.title: RoS confirms PN's deregistration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has confirmed that Perikatan Nasional's registration has been cancelled, saying the coalition's explanation failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice. RoS said the decision was made under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after reviewing all documents and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12. "After reviewing all documents and explanations submitted, the Registrar of Societies found that the reasons given failed to refute the grounds for cancellation of registration stated in the notice.

items.title: Malaysia has made no commitment to provide financing support to AirAsia, ministry says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial assistance to budget airline operator AirAsia, the finance ministry said, though it acknowledged concerns over the carrier's financial health following a jump in jet fuel prices. Reuters reported this month, citing sources, that AirAsia was in talks with the government over potential support. The airline's co-founder Tony Fernandes said the talks focused on aviation-related costs such as airport charges and fuel, not financial assistance.

items.title: Malaysia CPO tax waivers could lift plantation stocks as inventory hits record high
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's plantation sector could receive a timely boost if the government waives crude palm oil (CPO) export tax to help clear swelling inventories, restore export competitiveness and claw back market share from Indonesia. The waiver of CPO export tax will help Malaysia regain market share from Indonesia," he said in a note. Malaysia previously waived CPO export tax for six months in 2020.

items.title: In search for Amelia Earhart's plane, tantalising clue turns out to be tree debris
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: US-based explorers who travelled to a tiny South Pacific island seeking to conclusively solve the 1937 disappearance of famed aviator Amelia Earhart have determined that an object they suspected was wreckage from her plane was a cluster of washed-up trees. The objective was to determine whether an elongated, multi-pronged object detected in 2020 satellite imagery in the island's lagoon was a remnant of Earhart's long-missing twin-engine Lockheed Electra 10-E aeroplane. Quoting Earhart, he added: "You know, Amelia herself said, 'Adventure is worthwhile in itself.'"

items.title: France's unrest lays bare 'slow agony' of Macron's twilight months
items.summary: FRANCE'S worst bout of civil unrest in years has plunged President Emmanuel Macron's final months in office deeper into turmoil, exposing the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger with little money to spend, scant political capital and an increasingly fragile grip on public order. Macron came to power almost a decade ago promising to upend France's sclerotic political class, turbocharge economic reforms and restore authority through a more assertive presidency. "Le Pen no longer needs to spend any money to campaign," Jean-Baptiste Moreau, another former Macron lawmaker, told Reuters.

items.title: Dollar, euro drift as markets seek direction, yen slips
items.summary: The euro was steady at US$1.1216, while the British pound rose 0.1 per cent to US$1.3308. The Australian dollar gained 0.1 per cent to US$0.6986, while the New Zealand dollar edged up 0.1 per cent to US$0.5668. Against the yen, the US dollar was flat at 158.56 yen ahead of an auction of 20-year Japanese government bonds.

items.title: Perak smallholders suffer losses as elephants ravage oil palm plots
items.summary: SUNGAI SIPUT: Eighteen oil palm smallholders in Rancangan Tanah Belia Khas (RTBK) Kampung Perlop 1 here are facing mounting distress after a herd of wild elephants destroyed their crops spanning about 81 hectares since early September. One of the affected smallholders, Mastura Yusuf, 65, said her 12.1-ha plot suffered severe damage, with over 300 oil palm trees destroyed, particularly three-year-old saplings. She said the wild elephants also damaged farm infrastructure, including water storage containers and concrete water tanks.

items.title: Malaysia targets Smart Highway technology on half of expressways in the country, says works minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysia aims to equip at least 50 per cent of its 34 expressways with Smart Highway technology to enhance road safety, improve traffic flow and boost transport system efficiency. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the initiative would incorporate artificial intelligence (AI), smart closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems, and detection and early-warning systems for high-risk incidents, including accidents. “Malaysia is also prioritising the development of a National Intelligent Traffic Management Centre (NITMC) to strengthen real-time monitoring, integrated data analysis and traffic management coordination.

items.title: Hamzah expects Anwar to call GE16 by August next year amid Pakatan-Umno tensions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin expects Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to call the 16th general election by August next year, citing growing tensions between Pakatan Harapan and Umno, according to Free Malaysia Today (FMT). Speaking in an interview with BFM Radio, Hamzah said the unity government might struggle to remain intact beyond 2027, pointing to renewed scrutiny of Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s court cases by PH lawmakers. Hamzah, who leads Wawasan, suggested that the growing friction between the two political blocs could prompt Anwar to call an election before the coalition government fractures.

items.title: Temerloh police bust four gangs linked to ECRL, TM cable thefts in Pahang
items.summary: Temerloh police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said in a statement that between September and October this year, two robbery cases at ECRL cable storage facilities and five TM cable theft cases were reported around Temerloh, Mentakab, and Lanchang. Meanwhile, he said on October 14, police crippled Geng Kepala, believed to be involved in several Tenaga Nasional Berhad cable thefts at storage facilities, factories, and roadsides around Mentakab since August. “The suspect confessed to involvement in several TM cable thefts along roadsides around Mentakab since October this year, alongside another accomplice still at large,” he said.

items.title: Haze: Batu Muda, Johan Setia among 29 areas with unhealthy air quality
items.summary: Alor Gajah in Melaka recorded 155, while Bandaraya Melaka registered 152. In Perak, Tasek Ipoh recorded 155, followed by Pegoh Ipoh at 152. Meanwhile, 32 areas recorded moderate API readings.

items.title: Babysitter detained after 10-month-old baby boy dies in her care in Tasek Gelugor
items.summary: TASEK GELUGOR, Oct 20 — Police have detained a babysitter to assist in investigations into the death of a 10-month-old baby boy who was reported to have died while in the woman’s care here yesterday. Seberang Perai Utara district police chief ACP Anuar Abdul Rahman said the woman was detained following the incident and the case is being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001. The 25-year-old babysitter allegedly found the baby weak and lethargic at about 9.50 am and took him to a nearby clinic.

items.title: Penang police arrest six men over alleged abuse of Indonesian woman in Selangor
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Oct 20 — Police have detained six men to assist investigations into the abuse of an Indonesian woman in Tanjong Sepat, Selangor, in a raid at a business premise at Pusat Perniagaan Oren, Jalan Merbau, here today. Seberang Perai Utara district police chief ACP Anuar Abdul Rahman said the 6.30pm raid was carried out by the Selangor police contingent headquarters (IPK) Criminal Investigation Department (CID) team, with assistance from the Penang IPK CID team. Following the incident, police detained six men, including the woman’s employer, to assist in investigations into the case,” he said in a statement tonight.

items.title: Data centres’ power demand to hit 8.39GW by 2030, with Johor accounting for biggest share
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Peak electricity demand from the data centre industry in Peninsular Malaysia is projected to reach 8.39 gigawatts (GW) by 2030, based on the current electricity supply planning estimates, according to the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra). Petra said 45 data centres had been completed and were operational in Peninsular Malaysia as of August 2026, with a combined electricity supply capacity of 6.04GW. “However, actual water consumption by data centres currently reported to the National Water Services Commission stands at 63.90 MLD,” Petra said.

items.title: Lunas targets April 2027 delivery of first littoral combat ship to Royal Malaysian Navy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Lumut Naval Shipyard Sdn Bhd (Lunas) remains committed to delivering the first littoral combat ship (LCS1) to the Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN), with the target for physical delivery revised to April 2027. Lunas said the revised delivery timeline for LCS1 should be viewed in the context of the programme’s overall technical, regulatory and contractual complexities, and the ship’s delivery schedule was affected by the cancellation of the export licence for the surface-to-surface missile system by the Norwegian authorities as well. Following the decision, Lunas was no longer permitted under international export control regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), to deliver a ship equipped with the missile launcher system in question.

items.title: National Australia Bank to cut 2,500 jobs in cost overhaul as credit growth slows
items.summary: BENGALURU: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) will cut up to 2,500 jobs, or about six per cent of its workforce, over the next year to simplify operations and reduce costs amid pressure on Australia's credit growth. The bank, Australia's biggest business lender and third-largest home lender, said up to 1,500 positions would be cut by the end of 2026. NAB said it would begin consultations with the Finance Sector Union, whose national assistant secretary Nicole McPherson said the job cuts would not help simplify the organisation.

items.title: Nearly RM11b in STR, Sara aid disbursed as of September, says Finance Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Nearly RM11 billion in Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) assistance had been disbursed to eligible recipients as of September 2026, according to the Ministry of Finance (MoF). MoF said that RM3.6 billion had been disbursed to STR recipients through three payment phases as of last month. “This year, nearly nine million citizens are eligible to receive Sara monthly, while STR is distributed quarterly to eligible households and the elderly.

items.title: Police, activists move cats to safety after viral video sparks outrage
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH: Police and animal welfare activists have removed several cats from the home of a suspect arrested after a video showing him committing an indecent act involving a cat went viral. District police chief Superintendent Saari Yaacob said the animals were relocated to ensure their safety following the 49-year-old suspect's arrest at 10am yesterday. Saari said police are investigating the suspect's mental health status following claims that he has psychological issues.

items.title: Finance Ministry says no commitment to bail out AirAsia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Finance Ministry (MoF) has not made any commitment to provide financial assistance to AirAsia Bhd, whether in the form of guarantees, financing or injection of public funds. The ministry said applications for government support from any companies will be considered based on the interests of the country and the people, fiscal sustainability and the protection of public funds, in accordance with prevailing laws and procedures. The ministry said the government has taken note of issues raised concerning AirAsia, including the losses reported in its latest quarterly financial results.

items.title: Anwar: Govt refining haze plan, reviewing school closure measures
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is refining proposals to improve the National Haze Action Plan, particularly regarding school closure directives and the Ministry of Education’s (MOE) early preparations to ensure learning can continue if schools are forced to close. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, via a Facebook post yesterday, said the health of children remains the government’s top priority while ensuring their education is not disrupted. He said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Department of Environment, and the Malaysian Meteorological Department will refine these proposals together with the MOE and the Ministry of Health (MOH).

items.title: Oil eases as markets assess Russian energy waiver, Middle East supply risks
items.summary: BENGALURU: Oil prices fell on Tuesday as markets weighed an executive order by US President Donald Trump waiving some sanctions and tariffs linked to Russian energy exports, while attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemen kept concerns over Middle East supply disruptions in focus. Brent crude futures fell 49 cents, or 0.45 per cent, to US$109.06 a barrel by 8.10am Malaysian time. The US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude contract for November delivery, which expires on Tuesday, eased 0.33 per cent to US$103.32.

items.title: Vote count begins in Alberta secession referendum, testing Canadian unity
items.summary: EDMONTON: Vote counting was underway in Canada's province of Alberta on Monday, as the oil-rich province decided whether to hold a binding independence referendum, testing national unity amid a crisis in relations with the United States. Elections Alberta said 1.4 million of the 3.1 million eligible voters had cast advance ballots. Results might not be available until the early hours of Tuesday, Elections Alberta said.

items.title: Firefly to fully resume Subang-Singapore flights on Oct 22
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Oct 20 — Firefly will fully resume its flights between Subang and Singapore on Thursday (October 22), following its latest operational assessment of weather and haze conditions in Singapore. In an advisory on Monday, the airline said it would operate a reduced flight schedule between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport on October 21 before restoring full services the following day. “Affected passengers are being contacted and offered alternative travel arrangements on available Malaysia Airlines flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Singapore (SIN), subject to seat availability.

items.title: Woman killed as trailer runs red light, rams car in Machang
items.summary: MACHANG: A 26-year-old woman was killed when her car was rammed by a trailer that ran a red light at Km4.7 of Jalan Machang-Tanah Merah, near the Wakaf Bata traffic light junction, here last night. District police chief Superintendent Azuhar Md Nor said initial investigations revealed that the Volvo trailer, driven by a 47-year-old man, was travelling from Tanah Merah towards Machang. "The trailer driver was unhurt," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher as inflation eases, OPR normalisation in focus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Tuesday despite a stronger greenback, supported by easing domestic inflation and expectations of a possible normalisation of the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR). At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0780/0850 against the US dollar, compared with Monday's close of 4.0805/0845. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid expected the ringgit to trade within a range of RM4.07 to RM4.08 against the US dollar today.

items.title: Haze may ease by month-end as monsoon rains arrive - Academic
items.summary: Universiti Malaysia Perlis (Unimap) Faculty of Civil Engineering and Technology associate professor Dr Norazian Mohamed Noor said these factors could help reduce atmospheric pollutant concentrations and limit the cross-border movement of smoke from Indonesia. "These conditions offer a positive indication that increased rainfall could help improve air quality in Malaysia. "Haze conditions are influenced not only by rainfall in Malaysia but also by fire activity, rainfall distribution in pollution-source areas and wind direction.

items.title: Threatened with arrest, housewife loses RM472,000 to scammers
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 46-year-old housewife here lost RM472,000 after falling victim to a phone scam syndicate. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim lodged a police report at 10.30am yesterday. "The suspect impersonating Sergeant Andi instructed the victim to read out her identity card number.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: ‘Corporate mafia’, Felda abuse of power claims among issues to be raised
items.summary: According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official portal, during Minister’s Question Time, Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) will ask the Prime Minister for an update on “corporate mafia” allegations involving violations of the law and the action taken so far. Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) will ask the Prime Minister for an update on investigations into alleged misappropriation, corruption and abuse of power involving Felda, including its subsidiary Felda Investment Corporation. The sitting is scheduled to continue with the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill (Budget 2027), following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9.

items.title: 'Corporate mafia', abuse of power issues to take centre stage in Dewan Rakyat today
items.summary: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) is scheduled to ask the prime minister during Minister's Question Time about legal violations allegedly committed by a "corporate mafia" and the action taken so far, according to the Order Paper on Parliament's official portal. Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) will also ask the prime minister about the progress of investigations into alleged misappropriation, corruption and abuse of power involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation. The sitting will proceed with the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill (Budget 2027), tabled on Oct 9 by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after 43 years [WATCH]
items.summary: NEW YORK: Veteran journalist Christiane Amanpour said on Monday that she was leaving her role at CNN after a 43-year career as one of the US broadcaster's most prominent international correspondents. "After thinking carefully for several months and experiencing a few sleepless nights, as you can imagine, I've decided to separate from CNN," Amanpour, 68, said in a statement. Discovery, the parent company of CNN.

items.title: Ukraine claims US missile holdup as Trump floats summit without Zelenskyy
items.summary: Kyiv said it had received no early warning of powerful Russian missile strikes, echoing similar claims made last week. "The missiles are ready, and they could already be in Ukraine," Zelenskyy said. "Zelenskyy doesn't know what he's talking about," Trump said.

items.title: MBSB's transformation faces profitability test
items.summary: Chairman Datuk Wan Kamaruzaman Wan Ahmad acknowledged that legacy financing issues, integration challenges and fierce competition continue to weigh on earnings, despite improvements in the group's funding position and expansion of its financial services. MBSB's total assets rose 1.5 per cent to RM65.2 billion at the end of 2025 from RM64.3 billion in 2024, its first full financial year following the acquisition of Malaysian Industrial Development Finance Bhd (MIDF). He said shareholders supported management's cautious approach to deploying capital rather than pursuing aggressive financing growth to boost short-term profits.

items.title: University of North Carolina settles federal probes by Trump administration
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration has reached a settlement with the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill to close 18 federal probes into alleged race discrimination and antisemitism at the university. The agreement said UNC would appoint an internal administrator and establish a coordinator position in its compliance office to address discrimination, including antisemitism. It also requires UNC to provide mandatory antisemitism training for students, faculty and staff.

items.title: As midterms loom, Trump seizes on France unrest for political gain
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump used the protests roiling France to score quick political points on Monday, as the upcoming midterm elections leave his Republican Party facing strong headwinds. Speaking to reporters, Trump recalled an exchange with his French counterpart Emmanuel Macron: "I told him a long time ago, you're making a big mistake in France. Earlier on Monday, the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform: "The migrants have taken over France.

items.title: Australian lawmaker hurt in car attack underwent surgery overnight
items.summary: WANGARATTA: Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines underwent surgery overnight but remains in a critical condition after being deliberately struck by a car, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday. Political violence is rare in Australia, but law enforcement agencies have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed at the nation's elected officials in recent years. She was retrieving items from the boot of her car when the attack happened, Albanese said.

items.title: Posh cars put Kempas PPR tenants in spotlight [WATCH]
items.summary: The tenants live at the People's Housing Programme (PPR) project in Kempas, where a recent enforcement operation by the Johor State Housing Development Corporation (PKPJ) uncovered their vehicle ownership. Johor has 15,631 affordable rental homes under 14 PPR projects and eight Government Rental Housing (RSK) projects, managed by PKPJ for lower-income households. A further 348 termination notices and 55 eviction notices were issued after tenants ignored remedial notices.

items.title: Trump calls for renaming New Mexico 'New America'
items.summary: ISTANBUL: US President Donald Trump on Monday called for the southwestern state of New Mexico to be renamed "New America", arguing that the change would boost its prestige, property values and incomes, Anadolu Ajansi reported. "New Mexico should immediately change its name to New America. However, Trump cannot unilaterally rename a US state, as changing New Mexico's name would require amending its constitution.

items.title: In haze-hit Johor, staying indoors is a luxury delivery riders cannot afford
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — For delivery riders in Johor, escaping the thick haze that has settled over the state is not as simple as staying indoors. For Ghani Jaafar, a 50-year-old food and beverage delivery rider on the outskirts of Johor Bahru, the effects of the haze were difficult to ignore. Delivery rider Ghani Jaafar, 50, said he experienced a sore throat and nasal irritation after prolonged exposure to the haze in Johor last week.

items.title: Not sympathy, but opportunity: Push grows for fairer hiring of visually impaired Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — It is not a lack of talent, but rather stigma and doubts about their capabilities that continue to hinder persons with visual impairments from entering the job market, including the creative arts industry. Malaysian Association for the Blind (MAB) chief executive officer Datuk George Thomas told Bernama that misconceptions among employers about the capabilities of persons with visual impairments remained prevalent, undermining their chances of securing jobs based on their qualifications and talents. The programme, organised by MAB in collaboration with the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), aimed to raise employers’ awareness of the actual capabilities of persons with visual impairments.

items.title: US set to announce certification of Boeing 737 MAX 10 on Tuesday
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is expected to announce on Tuesday that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has approved the Boeing 737 MAX 10 during a visit to Washington state, sources briefed on the plans told Reuters. Duffy is set to appear at a Boeing factory in Everett, Washington, to announce the FAA certification of the long-delayed larger variant of Boeing's best-selling aircraft. Boeing opened a new production line at the Everett plant in July to expand 737 MAX production.

items.title: Zahid calls for cabinet paper on motorcycle safety
items.summary: THE Transport Ministry and the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (Miros) will prepare a cabinet paper on motorcycle safety, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Zahid was speaking at the Conference on Asia Road Safety (CARS) 2026, held with Transport Expo Asia 2026, organised by Miros here. Zahid said Malaysia must strengthen coordination and sustain road safety efforts to achieve its target of reducing road fatalities by 50 per cent by 2030.

items.title: Trump says Washington golf course project to start immediately, despite judge's order
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that his administration would begin renovation work immediately on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior notification to the court. The renovation work, which Trump said a day earlier would start next month, has become the subject of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns. Earlier this year, he said work would begin in September.

items.title: Tiger footprints found at Perak farm
items.summary: THE Perak Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has confirmed the discovery of tiger footprints at a farm near Jalan Air Betang-Jalan Kampung Air Panas, Gerik, last Wednesday. "The orchard is about 2km from the Bintang Hijau Forest Reserve," said Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah yesterday. Images of the footprints have gone viral, raising concerns among residents.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt to study identity, age checks for Roblox and online gaming platforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The government will examine the feasibility of expanding the implementation of electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) verification and age verification to online gaming platforms such as Roblox, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the move will take into account various aspects, including issues involving underage users as well as the possibility of the platforms being abused by extremist, radical, and terrorist groups. The issue might only be in terms of user verification and user age verification.

items.title: Malaysia, Japan explore defence technology transfer, local industry cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Malaysia and Japan have the potential to expand defence industry cooperation through technology transfer, local component development and participation in global supply chains, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. “I received a briefing on Japan’s approach to developing its defence industry, while exchanging views on potential cooperation in technology transfer, local component development and global supply chains. “I believe closer ties based on trust and mutual respect will open up more opportunities for defence cooperation that benefit both countries,” he posted on X, explaining that ATLA was an agency under Japan’s Ministry of Defence responsible for defence procurement, technology and logistics.

items.title: Johor police arrest 13 over Molotov cocktail attack on Myanmar refugee homes in Kulai
items.summary: Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police nabbed the suspects, aged between 16 and 31, in Kulai district in an operation conducted from October 14 until yesterday. He said the Johor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) Criminal Investigation Department (CID), together with the Kulai District Police Headquarters (IPD) CID, carried out the arrests based on public information. Ab Rahaman said police remanded four suspects for eight days beginning October 14, four for a week, and one for five days beginning October 15, while remanding four others for a week starting today.

items.title: Budget 2027 debate: Calls for fairer MP allocations, faster migrant deportations and tax relief for caregivers
items.summary: Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) urged the government to enact legislation to ensure constituency allocations for MPs were distributed according to a proportional formula based on the number of voters and residents, regardless of political affiliation. Other constituencies, meanwhile, have only half or a third of Bangi’s number of voters. “Many people want to care for their parents at home and provide personal care.

items.title: Kelantan police arrest man over alleged indecent act involving cat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — A man has been arrested in Kelantan to assist investigations into a viral video allegedly showing him committing an indecent act involving a cat at his home. Pasir Puteh district police chief Superintendent Saari Yaacob said police received a report on October 18 after the video circulated on social media platform Threads. He said police subsequently arrested a man to assist with further investigations, with the case being investigated under Section 377 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

items.title: ‘Justice has prevailed’: Teresa Kok wins RM250,000 defamation suit against Dr Akmal over halal certification row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Seputeh MP Teresa Kok has won RM250,000 in damages in her defamation suit against Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh over remarks he made during a dispute on halal certification. In a statement posted on Facebook, Kok said she hoped the judgment would serve as a reminder that democratic freedoms must be exercised responsibly. “I hope this judgment serves as a reminder that democratic freedoms must be exercised responsibly.

items.title: Selangor Sultan launches Silver Jubilee book, stamps and coins marking 25 years on throne
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 19 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah today launched a commemorative book, first-day cover and stamps, and special coins in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’s reign. Also present at the ceremony at Pustaka Raja Tun Uda here were Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin and Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah. Accompanied by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, Sultan Sharafuddin officiated at the launch of the commemorative items, presented as tokens of appreciation by the Selangor government in collaboration with the Selangor State Treasury, Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) and Pos Malaysia Bhd.

items.title: Proposed Kuching international airport could contribute RM1.8b annually to Sarawak GDP by 2050, says state minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 19 — The proposed New Kuching International Airport (NKIA) at Tanjung Embang could contribute approximately RM1.8 billion annually to Sarawak’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2050 under a high-growth scenario. “The study also projected that NKIA could support approximately 37,919 full-time equivalent jobs across the wider economy. During construction, Phase One could support around 9,393 jobs annually over the projected six-year construction period.

items.title: AGC to appeal against Session Court’s decision to acquit and discharge Papagomo of sedition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will file a notice of appeal against the Sessions Court’s decision to acquit and discharge blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, of a sedition charge. In a statement today, the AGC said the decision was made after examining the ruling of the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court sitting in the Klang Sessions Court today, which acquitted and discharged Wan Muhammad Azri, 43, at the close of the defence case for a charge under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948 (Act 15). “The accused presented his defence by giving sworn testimony in the same Sessions Court.

items.title: Semporna’s illegal foreign business activities raised in Cabinet, says minister
items.summary: SEMPORNA, Oct 19 — The issue of foreigners abusing social visit passes to engage in illegal economic activities in Semporna has been raised and discussed in the Federal Cabinet, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud. “Action is being taken on this issue, with operations conducted particularly against business activities on the islands. “The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) has also discussed this issue and will take appropriate action,” he told reporters after an official working visit today to assess border control preparedness at Pulau Ligitan, Pulau Sipadan and Pulau Mabul.

items.title: Sabah registers 38,659 commercial vehicles under subsidised diesel scheme
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 19 — A total of 38,659 commercial vehicles belonging to 17,703 companies in Sabah have registered under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) as of yesterday, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali He said the registrations comprised 27,655 vehicles transporting essential goods, 8,773 company-owned vehicles, including jeeps and pick-up trucks, and 2,231 public land transport vehicles. Armizan said 1,408 vehicles belonging to 995 companies in Sabah had also registered under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS). These comprised 788 public land transport vehicles and 620 vehicles transporting essential goods.

items.title: Sarawak targets 15,000MW power capacity by 2035, with 60pc from renewables
items.summary: “The Baleh hydroelectric plant, with a capacity of 1,285 MW, is expected to operate in the fourth quarter of 2029. The Samalaju CCPP, with a capacity of 1,500 MW, is scheduled to operate in phases, with Blocks 1 and 2 having a total capacity of 1,000 MW expected to operate in the second quarter of 2027, while Block 3 with a capacity of 500 MW is scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. “Currently, Sarawak exports an average of 100 MW to West Kalimantan and 30 MW to Sabah.

items.title: Malaysia retains WHO validation for eliminating mother-to-child HIV, syphilis transmission
items.summary: In a statement, the Ministry of Health (MOH) said the achievement reaffirmed the recognition first obtained in 2018, when Malaysia became the first country in the WHO Western Pacific Region to receive the validation. The ministry said the recognition reflected Malaysia’s continued commitment to strengthening maternal and child health and ensuring access to quality screening, treatment and healthcare services. According to the MOH, screening coverage for HIV and syphilis among pregnant women remained above 95 per cent throughout the assessment period, while antiretroviral treatment coverage among pregnant women living with HIV reached approximately 99 per cent.

items.title: Data Centre Bill to go to Cabinet in 2027, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the measure aims to ensure that investments in the industry add value to the domestic economy, in addition to addressing utility constraints and avoiding imbalances in environmental impact. He said the agreement was reached following the presentation of the National Strategic Direction Towards Sustainable Data Centre Development by the Ministry of Digital. Akmal Nasrullah said NEAC also agreed that the four lead ministries, along with the implementing agencies, would adopt the Circular Economy Framework (CEF) presented by the Ministry of Economy.

items.title: Rapid KL to deploy 85 shuttle buses for Malaysian GP at Sepang
items.summary: Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the service was aimed at meeting the transport needs of motorsports fans and facilitating their journeys to the circuit. He said tickets would go on sale from October 22 at selected customer service counters and the Pasar Seni Bus Hub. Syahrul Azmir said the shuttle service would operate from three main locations, namely the Pasar Seni Bus Hub, the KLCC bus stop and the KLIA Terminal 2 Bus Hub.
